title: Decomposed Relation Extraction from Aviation Accident Narratives: Evaluating Transformer-Based Safety Knowledge Discovery under Relational Sparsity
abstract: arXiv:2610.27013v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Relation extraction from aviation accident narratives is challenging because genuine safety relations are sparse among possible concept pairs. This study evaluates a decomposed framework separating relation classification from concept identification. A benchmark of 300 National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) narratives containing 2,524 unique concept-text nodes was expanded into 21,038 ordered candidate pairs, with only 248 (1.18%) representing RESULTS_IN or CONTRIBUTES_TO relations. A TF-IDF Linear Support Vector Machine (SVM) and weighted RoBERTa classifier were developed using an independent graph-annotated resource with hard-negative sampling and frozen before sealed evaluation. Development Macro-F1 scores of 0.4738 (SVM) and 0.4809 (RoBERTa) declined to 0.2741 and 0.2420 under exhaustive evaluation, with Matthews correlation coefficients of 0.0128 and 0.0197. translated_title: 航空事故叙述文本的分解式关系抽取：关系稀疏性下基于Transformer的安全知识发现评估
translated_abstract: 从航空事故叙述文本中进行关系抽取极具挑战性，因为真正的安全关系在所有可能的概念对中非常稀疏。本研究评估了一种将关系分类与概念识别相分离的分解式框架。研究构建了一个包含300篇美国国家运输安全委员会（NTSB）叙述文本的基准数据集，其中含有2,524个独特的概念-文本节点，并将其扩展为21,038个有序候选对，其中仅有248个（1.18%）代表RESULTS_IN或CONTRIBUTES_TO关系。研究者使用一个独立的图标注资源（结合困难负样本采样）开发了TF-IDF线性支持向量机（SVM）和加权RoBERTa分类器，并在密封评估前冻结了模型参数。开发阶段的Macro-F1分数分别为0.4738（SVM）和0.4809（RoBERTa），而在穷举评估中下降至0.2741和0.2420，马修斯相关系数分别为0.0128和0.0197。假阳性占主导地位：SVM恢复了96个参考关系，但……
tldr: 该研究提出将概念识别与关系分类相分离的分解式框架，并在NTSB事故叙述的大规模稀疏基准上系统评估发现，SVM与RoBERTa模型在真实关系稀疏场景下性能急剧下降（Macro-F1从约0.48降至约0.24-0.27），揭示了现有关系抽取方法在航空安全知识发现中面临的严重挑战。
en_tdlr: This study proposes a decomposed framework separating concept identification from relation classification and reveals through large-scale sparse benchmark evaluation on NTSB accident narratives that both SVM and RoBERTa models suffer severe performance degradation under real-world relational sparsity, highlighting critical challenges for transformer-based safety knowledge discovery.
